I farm 10.1 mu under a wheat-maize rotation, so I will put the full 10.1 mu into winter wheat first and then summer maize on the same land after wheat harvest. I have been farming a long time, I have well irrigation, and some people in my family work off-farm, so I will keep my plan steady and practical rather than complicated. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give enough nitrogen as the main driver of yield, add phosphorus and some potassium to keep the stand strong, irrigate at the key stages, and use rotary tillage because it fits my usual way of preparing land after maize. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because it gives me stronger yield on irrigated land, keep fertilizer at a moderate but solid level, reduce tillage pressure by going with no-tillage after wheat harvest so I can sow quickly, and rely on a few irrigations and basic pest control. My goal is stable grain yield from both crops with work intensity that my household can actually manage.
